name: G#
title: G# (0.5.212)
lifecycleNote: v0.5.212 (2026-10-22) is the current published release; the 0.5 line self-hosted from v0.5.3, and the 'Next' docs are development documentation, not a release

type.text: **`T?` is a distinct type with `nil`, `?.`, `??`, `??=`, and flow narrowing**: `if let`, `guard let`, and `while let` strip the nullable layer, and a violated non-null assumption fails at a written `!!`
**Null-safety gate at the call site**: a nullable value at a non-nullable parameter is an error (`GS0154`), so an imported `T!` (platform) reference cannot flow unchecked into a non-null position
**Generics are reified end to end**: `GenericParam` rows, `TypeSpec` encodings, and closed instantiations land in the emitted metadata, so a type argument survives into the artifact
**A package scopes names, imports are selective, and visibility is declared**: `package`, `import` (+ aliases and per-file static imports), and `public`/`internal`/`private` are real boundaries

**Polymorphism without an inheritance chain**: interfaces with default methods and static-virtual slots, explicit qualifiers `func (IFoo) M`, and `adapt[I](source)` structural adaptation; classes are sealed unless declared `open`
**Payload-bearing enums are discriminated unions**: `enum Shape { Circle(r float64); Square(s float64) }`, sealed hierarchies, and pattern switches the compiler checks for exhaustiveness

**The numeric lattice is width-named**: canonical `int8`–`int64`/`uint8`–`uint64` names with binder-resolved friendly aliases; lossless widening, explicit `T(x)` narrowing, constant-expression narrowing only as in C#

**Reflection reaches private members through the ordinary .NET runtime APIs, and `object` boxes any value**, so a declared boundary is not a ceiling; the charge rests on this reflective reach, the half the C# page also charges — the erasure half does not apply here (see the reified-generics bullet above)
**Signatures carry no effect set**: a `throw` needs no declaration, and a call's I/O, mutation, suspension, and lock footprint is read from its body

**`await` colours the function that spells it**: the function compiles to a `ValueTask` state machine, `suspend func` pins the shape at fixed-shape signatures, and a suspending call made from a plain function blocks with warning `GS0558`
**`@DllImport`/`@LibraryImport`, `@MarshalAs`, and unmanaged function pointers are hand-written ABI promises**: layout, marshalling, lifetime, and calling convention land outside the type system

construction.text: **Every binding states its kind**: `const` (compile-time constant), `let` (immutable binding), `var` (mutable); the form is spelled per site, not defaulted
**`let` freezes the rebinding, not the graph behind it**: the referenced value stays writable, so write permission is read from the declaration form the team chooses

**Value aggregates build in place**: struct literals, `adapt[I](ref handle)`, `slice[T]` views, `stackalloc`, and structural projection `Target{ ...source, Member: override }` construct over storage the caller chose
**`data class`/`data struct` synthesize equality, deconstruction, and `with`-copy** (C# record ABI since 0.5, ADR-0199); classes carry primary constructors and `init` blocks

memory.text: **The CLR garbage collector decides when memory returns**: the release schedule belongs to the runtime, not to the program
**A `managed[T]` handle provides GC reachability, not exclusivity, synchronization, native ownership or race freedom; a `slice[T]` view retains the entire owner array**
**`using let` binds a disposable to scope exit, and `defer call(...)` schedules a call at scope exit** with a cancellation grace budget

**The by-ref discipline is a scope rule, not an ownership analysis**: `ref`/`out`/`in`/`scoped` parameters, ref locals and ref returns are checked by a simple non-escaping rule; the full ref-safe-to-escape analysis is not implemented

error.text: **Failures are CLR exceptions with no signature list**: no `throws` clause exists, so the set of failures a call can raise is discovered on the path that raises it
**`try`/`catch`/`finally` with four catch forms, `when` filters emitted as real CLR filter regions, and `rethrow`**: a detected failure travels to a handler through a language construct

**The shipped `Gsharp.Extensions.Optional` composes `T?` through expressions**: `Map`, `FlatMap`, `OrElse`, `OrCompute`, `IfPresent`, `Filter`, and `OrThrow` carry the absent value as a value (`Gsharp.Extensions` is referenced automatically; imports stay explicit per file)

concurrency.text: **A `go` task shares the parent's heap by default**: closures capture the enclosing bindings, and a plain `map[K,V]` is explicitly not goroutine-safe

**The ordering discipline lives outside the type**: the concurrency guide prescribes `lock`, `SyncMap[K,V]`, and BCL concurrent types, and nothing proves the discipline or detects a missing lock; the project's own contract checks are named as the substitute for a race detector

**`scope { }` joins its `go` children before control moves on**, cancels siblings on first failure, and aggregates failures as a `ScopeException`; an `async let` binding cannot be stored, returned, or collected
**Channels, `select`, and directional `in`/`out` handles are language constructs with no import**: `chan[T]` **is** `System.Threading.Channels.Channel<T>`

platform.text: **The language has one implementation**: a bespoke self-hosted compiler (written in G# since 0.5.3) with Roslyn deliberately kept out of the compiler process (ADR-0027); `cs2gs` migrates C# source, it is not a second compiler, so every consumer works on one compiler's release cycle

**The emitted artifact is standard ECMA-335 PE with Portable PDB**: it runs on CoreCLR and Mono, on Windows, Linux, and macOS, and the compiler cross-targets net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 through an isolated metadata-load context

performance.text: **GC pauses are part of the timing budget**: server and background GC modes bound the pause and do not remove it, and the collector decides when it arrives
**The CLR tiers its compilation**, so the first requests measure slower than steady state and a benchmark has to agree on a warm-up

**Every driver emits CIL**: the single-file `gsc` run, the `gsi` REPL, and the SDK build share the emitter; the tree-walking evaluator was removed, and the emitted executable is the differential oracle for the other drivers

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem is young and small**: 55 releases since the first alpha (2026-05-29), six first-party NuGet packages, and a handful of third-party G# libraries, so a G# project more often writes what it needs than finds it, and the hiring market is correspondingly small
**The library supply behind it is .NET's**: any NuGet package is reachable through interop, and the guide's rule is to use CLR interop instead of wrappers
**CLR metadata carries a published promise**: G# compiles to IL under the runtime's standardised format [@ecma335; @dotnetCompat]

evolution.text: **Pre-1.0 evolution reaches the source**: the 0.5 line retired the `chan T` spelling (`GS0567`), the Go-style built-ins (`GS0566`), `record` (`GS0535`), and `:=` (`GS0305`), and array length became part of the type, so a program written on 0.4 is edited, not recompiled, on 0.5

**What changed: 0.5 adopted the C# record ABI for `data class` and `data struct` (ADR-0199), so the synthesized `ToString`, equality, and `PrintMembers` output of unchanged source changed with the toolchain; a `record`-shaped consumer that prints a data type sees the 0.4 text until it edits. Why: interop parity with C# consumers — the record shape is what BCL and C# code already understands. How a deployment reverses it: pin the toolchain to a pre-0.5 release (the compatibility policy instructs pinning exact versions for production), which restores the 0.4 synthesized surface; a pinned deployment never sees the change**

domain.text: **The target is ordinary .NET application work**: console, library, web, and TUI samples ship in the templates, and the Trail tutorial builds a worker-pool inventory app from the language's own constructs

learning.text: **Several paradigms arrive at once**: Go-shaped concurrency, Kotlin/Swift-shaped data and nullability, CLR-shaped members, and the `unsafe`/span/ref machinery; one shape can be modelled as `struct`, `data struct`, `data class`, `inline struct`, anonymous object, or `adapt[I]` wrapper, so "the way we do it here" is a written team convention the language will not narrow

**The reference material is unusually complete for a pre-1.0 language**: a normative specification with an EBNF appendix, a 512-ID `GS####` diagnostics catalogue with cause and remedy per ID, a feature matrix with explicit Partial and Removed rows, four bridge guides (C#, Go, Kotlin, Swift), and 215 recorded ADRs

testing.text: **The official distribution ships a test path**: `Gsharp.Templates` includes a `gsharp-xunit` template, the SDK integrates with `dotnet test`, and the Visual Studio extension carries native Test Explorer for xUnit, NUnit, and MSTest

**Debugging runs on Portable PDBs through the official VS Code and Visual Studio extensions** (`coreclr` debug resolution, F5 managed debugging), with `dotnet watch` hot reload and a logical view for suspending functions

security.text: **A lambda converts to `Expression[TDelegate]` when the target demands it**, so a G# program can build and compile code at run time (unsupported shapes diagnose `GS0473`)
**Memory safety is the CLR's**: `unsafe`, `stackalloc`, and `cast[ptr](addr)` bypass it by design — an opt-in escape hatch

**There is no `eval` facility and the evaluator backend was removed from the compiler**: the only run-time code path is the typed expression tree the source writes, recorded by the `Q3` mark — G# builds no code from untyped text

tradeoffs: **Nullability checking is a compiler option**: `/nullability:enabled|platform-types|oblivious` sets the enforcement level per compilation, so a project states its own contract — the incremental adoption path C# used

**Pre-1.0 churn is managed by a written policy**: diagnostic IDs are never reused, retired spellings ship replacement diagnostics, breaking changes require an ADR plus migration guidance, and production is told to pin exact versions
**The language-defined library stays deliberately small**, so BCL interop carries the everyday APIs; the guide's rule is "use CLR interop instead of wrappers"

**Concurrency inherits the Go shape — `go`, channels, `select` — onto CLR channel primitives**: a language-level spawn with `chan[T]` identical to `System.Threading.Channels.Channel<T>` (adapters stay spare), paid in rendezvous and capacity decisions a plain `spawn` never asks

**Data types adopted the C# record ABI in 0.5 (ADR-0199)**: C# interop parity gained, the 0.4 synthesized text surface spent — a trade the author pays per program, not a mechanism the inventory prices

**One compiler by design**: a bespoke ECMA-335 emitter with no Roslyn in the compiler process buys independence from the platform's compiler stack, paid in owning the metadata writer, the PDB writer, and the binder end to end
verdict: G# outscores the C# page on Core coupling (73.7 against 72.3; F# stays ahead of both): the constructs the inventory prices in its managed neighbours are the ones G# supplies — tasks joined by a `scope`, null checked by the type, payload enums with checked exhaustiveness, reified generics, declared module boundaries, `defer` and `using` release, deterministic emit, and a public specification. What it keeps is the platform's invoice: the GC's schedule and pauses, tiered compilation, function colouring (aggravated by inference), unchecked exceptions, and the hand-written ABI of P/Invoke. Its own youth is priced too: one compiler, a pre-1.0 contract, a small supply of libraries, solo governance, and no portable target. Main strengths: structured concurrency and nullability are language facts, and the documentation (spec, diagnostics catalogue, feature matrix, ADRs) is stronger than most post-1.0 languages. Main weaknesses: most of what sits below the Core score is ecosystem and governance, and those take years to buy.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green]. The project's own compile-time measurements (self-host parity 1.04x time, ReadyToRun payload +31% on hello-world compiles) are reported with their provenance and expiry stated on the page.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse corpus: the first public release (2026-05-29) postdates the training data of public coding models, so models write it unreliably; the bridge guides and the `cs2gs` pipeline exist precisely because human C# and Go experience transfers better than model output.

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: IL and assembly metadata follow a published standard, and the runtime publishes its compatibility rules
